---
description: "Delegate coding work to Cursor cloud agents: when to hand off, how to write the prompt, what to do when the host wakes you because one stopped, and how to look an agent up by id, read what it did, reply, and cancel."
---

# Cloud agent handoff

Hand work to a Cursor cloud agent when it needs a repository checkout, a long run, or an isolated machine: implementing a change, running a test suite, opening a pull request. Answer questions and small reads yourself.

The tools below are this extension's; they appear under its mount namespace, as `<namespace>__launch` and so on. Every agent is addressed by its `agent_id` (`bc-...`).

## Launch

Call `launch` with a self-contained prompt: the goal, the repository or pull request, constraints (branch, files to leave alone), and what done looks like (tests pass, PR opened). Pass `starting_ref` or `pr_url` to pick a branch or pull request; `repo` must be one of the configured repositories.

The result carries `agentId` (`bc-...`) and a `url`. Report both in full. Never truncate the id. With `watching: true`, the host watches the run and wakes this conversation once when it stops, so you do not need to poll it.

## When an agent stops

The wake is a message that starts with `[cloud agent stopped]`, followed by the agent's details in the shape `get` returns; its `status` is `finished`, `error`, or `expired`. Read the report with `dump` before you tell anyone what the agent did, then share the pull request or the error. The host stops watching without a wake when the agent can no longer be read or is still running after a day; if you are asked about an agent you have not heard back from, look it up with `get`.

## Look an agent up by id

Call `get` with the `agent_id`. It returns the agent's `status` (`creating`, `running`, `finished`, `error`, `expired`, or `unknown`), its `branch` and pull request `prUrl` once pushed, change counts, a `summary` when one exists, and an `error` when it failed. A run takes minutes: check when asked or when you need the result before the wake, not in a loop. The final report itself comes from `dump`.

## Read what it did

To read the report or understand what was done, call `dump` with the `agent_id`. Once a transcript exists, it writes the agent's whole conversation to `cloud-agent-transcripts/<agent_id>.jsonl` in your workspace and returns the absolute `path` plus `finalMessage`. Before any transcript exists, either value may be absent; wait for output instead of inventing a report.

Use `finalMessage` as the agent's report. Read the returned transcript path when you need its prompts, reasoning, or tool calls, then inspect the resulting branch or pull request before claiming exact code changes. The transcript is evidence of what the agent did, not a canonical diff.

## Reply

Call `reply` with the `agent_id` and a prompt to steer an agent or ask for changes on its branch. The follow-up queues behind the current run and starts when it finishes; pass `interrupt: true` to stop the current step and deliver it now. The host does not watch a follow-up run; check it with `get` when you need its result. Do not launch a second agent for follow-up work on the same branch.

## Cancel

Call `cancel` with the `agent_id` to stop the active run; no stop wake follows. The agent keeps its branch and conversation, so a `reply` can continue from where it stopped.

## Fleet

`list` returns the agents launched in this session, newest first; pass `scope: "all"` to include your launches from other sessions. Launch one agent per independent task and give each a descriptive `name`. Agents launched by others are out of reach.
